questions.q: What three attributes define a single installment within a payment term?
options: Due percentage, days (or a fixed date), and date basis
Customer name, invoice number, and currency
Tax rate, freight amount, and discount rate only
Ledger, business unit, and transaction type
questions.explain: Each installment specifies what portion is due, how many days (or what fixed date) it's due by, and the anchor date basis those days count from.

questions.q: What is the most common date basis used to calculate a due date?
options: The receipt date
The transaction (invoice) date
The customer's credit review date
The general ledger period close date
questions.explain: The transaction date is the most common anchor, though ship date or other system-derived dates can also serve as the date basis.

questions.q: In the 50/50 Net 30/60 example, what does Receivables create for the single $10,000 invoice?
options: Two separate invoices for $5,000 each
One invoice that is only payable in full after 60 days
One invoice with two independently aged scheduled payments
A credit memo for half the amount
questions.explain: A split payment term produces multiple scheduled payments against the one transaction, each with its own due date, rather than creating multiple transactions.

questions.q: On a 2/10 Net 30 term for a $10,000 invoice dated March 1, what happens if the customer pays on March 20?
options: They still get the 2% discount because it's before the 30-day due date
The invoice is automatically written off
A chargeback is automatically created
The discount window has closed, so the full $10,000 is due
questions.explain: The 2% discount only applies within the discount window (10 days). Paying after that window means the full amount is owed by the net due date.

questions.q: Why do payment terms matter beyond just the invoice itself?
options: They determine when a balance becomes overdue, which drives aging reports and dunning
They have no effect outside the single transaction
They only affect which language the invoice prints in
They control which customer can be merged with another
questions.explain: Due dates calculated from payment terms feed directly into aging buckets and collections/dunning decisions for overdue balances.
